audit.whatIsWrong: The stored chart disagreed with its own whys in five of seven rows: why[0] describes mini-Gnar out-ranging you but the row said Skill, why[4] and why[5] describe Cho'Gath's Feast and tank spikes but the rows said Skill and Gnar, and why[6] says 'it evens back out' under a Gnar row.
audit.why: Mini-Gnar owns 1-2 on Boomerang Throw (1100 range) and Hop spacing; 3 through 5 is even once Carnivore and Vorpal Spikes waveclear come online; 6 and first item are Cho'Gath's on Feast and HP; two items is even because GNAR! decides teamfights.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Skill, matching the packet chart and the existing whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer phase why was the generic template — 'Gnar's ultimate changes the math too', no ability named, no cooldown given.
audit.why: Feast is 80/70/60s true damage and permanent max HP; it kills a sub-threshold mini-Gnar but not a Rage-form Mega pool. GNAR! is 90/60/30s — a 90-second cooldown at rank 1 is a real window, and it shrinks to 30s at rank 3, which is why the two-item stage stays even.
audit.corrected: Phase whys now name Boomerang Throw, Hop (22s), Wallop (7s), GNAR! (90s) and Feast (80s) with the mini-versus-Mega distinction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer tracked 'GNAR! (Mega Stun)' as the matchup-defining cooldown and never mentioned Hop, Wallop, or the reason Rupture whiffs. It also called GNAR! a stun outright.
audit.why: Rupture (Q, 950 range, flat 6s) has a cast delay and Gnar's Hop (E, 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s) is a dash that leaves the circle — Hop's 22s at rank 1 is the real punish window. Mega Wallop (W) is the flat-7s stun that beats your walk-up. GNAR! only stuns enemies thrown into a wall; in open ground it is a knockup and slow, so 'Mega Stun' is conditional on terrain.
audit.corrected: Rupture whiffs on Hop and Wallop's stun beats your walk-up — catch him mid-Hop, silence, then Feast.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Engage only on GNAR!'s cooldown' is unusable advice — GNAR! only exists while he is in Mega form.
audit.why: Hop at 22s rank 1 is the cooldown you can actually count in mini form, and it is what decides whether Rupture connects.
audit.corrected: Focus target moved to Gnar Hop and Wallop.

edits.before: Farm with E spikes and respect everything — you scale, he rents. Identify how Gnar contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Mini-Gnar's Boomerang Throw returns for a double hit and his Hop autos out-range you — hug the wave and last-hit with Vorpal Spikes.

edits.before: W silence starts flipping his combo windows. Only take the trade when Gnar's GNAR! is down.
edits.after: He pokes free while Rupture whiffs on his Hop (22s at rank 1) — his most abusable window.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gnar must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Carnivore starts healing the poke but he still chips from 1100 range on Boomerang Throw — a genuine coin-flip stretch.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around GNAR!'s cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Vorpal Spikes waveclear and Q rank-ups let you farm through it, but he keeps spacing — neither side runs it down here.

edits.before: Feast stacks turn you into terrain — every R is permanent HP plus a true-damage execute. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gnar's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast (80s) is a flat true-damage execute that ignores his armour and MR — a mini-Gnar below the threshold dies, but it will not delete Mega.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on GNAR!'s cooldown.
edits.after: Heartsteel plus Carnivore lets you eat the poke and bank Feast stacks under tower.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Gnar carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: It evens back out — you are the frontline, but one GNAR! wall-stun (90s at rank 1) into your backline is just as decisive.

edits.before: Track Gnar's GNAR! (Mega Stun): His Mega all-in. Q-zone mini form. When it is down — Q-W + R him.
edits.after: Rupture whiffs on Hop and Wallop's stun beats your walk-up — catch him mid-Hop, silence, then Feast.

edits.before: - Gnar GNAR!: matchup-defining — His Mega all-in. Q-zone mini form. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gnar Hop/Crunch: matchup-defining — 22s at rank 1 is the only window in which he cannot space you. Mega Wallop stuns on a flat 7s and GNAR! is 90s at rank 1. - Feast: never on chip, kill windows only.

edits.before: Q under Gnar's feet as he commits, W-silence the answer, and E-spike the trade — your sustain regens what his chip cost.
edits.after: Catch him mid-Hop with Rupture, Feral Scream the answer, then E-spike — his 22s E is the only thing that gets him out.

notes: GNAR! is described by Riot as a throw that stuns only enemies who hit a wall; the entry called it a flat 'Mega Stun', which is wrong in open ground. Cho'Gath's kit file flags Rupture (Q) as 'grounding' but Riot's text says it pops enemies into the air — treated as a knockup throughout. The content layer for this matchup was already accurate on names and mechanics; almost all the damage was in the full layer, which was untouched template text.
